title: Topology and closed subsets of a smooth stack presentation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Its points are maps $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal X$ from fields modulo isomorphism after common field extension. For a smooth surjective scheme atlas $q:V\to\mathcal X$, give $|\mathcal X|$ the quotient topology from $|V|$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. This topology is independent of the atlas, every stack morphism induces a continuous map, and $|q|$ is an open surjection. Put $R=V\times_{\mathcal X}V$, with projections $s,t$. The fibres of $|q|$ are exactly the equivalence classes given by the image of $(|s|,|t|):|R|\to|V|\times|V|$. Inverse image by $|q|$ bijects closed subsets of $|\mathcal X|$ with closed subsets $D\subseteq|V|$ satisfying $|s|^{-1}D=|t|^{-1}D$. Each closed subset $C\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ is the underlying subset of a unique reduced closed substack (a full substack whose pullback to every scheme is a closed subscheme, with reduced smooth charts). Finally, for any two morphisms of algebraic stacks $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$, the map $|\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C|\to|\mathcal A|\times_{|\mathcal B|}|\mathcal C|$ is surjective. In particular set-theoretic images commute with base change: the image of $|\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C|\to|\mathcal C|$ is the inverse image of the image of $|\mathcal A|\to|\mathcal B|$. All fibre products here are 2-fibre products.

source.place: Tags 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian), 04XJ (lemma-points-presentation), 04XL (lemma-topology-points), and 0509 (lemma-reduced-closed-substack). Closed-subset correspondence is the closed-set formulation of the quotient topology and the presentation equivalence relation.

proof.text: First prove the point assertion for arbitrary $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\leftarrow\mathcal C$. These 2-fibre products are algebraic stacks by the cited fibre-product node. Represent a pair of point classes with equal image by objects $a$ over a field $K$ and $c$ over a field $L$. Equality of the images means, by the point equivalence relation, that some common extension $M$ carries an isomorphism between their images in $\mathcal B(M)$. The triple $(a_M,c_M,\alpha)$ is exactly an object of the 2-fibre product over $M$, by its defining groupoid. Its point maps to the prescribed pair. Consequently a point of $\mathcal C$ is in the base-changed image precisely when its image in $\mathcal B$ is represented by some point of $\mathcal A$: both implications follow by projecting this triple. This proves surjectivity and the image/base-change assertion, without any injectivity claim.

source.place: Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian), field-triple proof; last assertion by projecting the pair.

proof.text: The topology node gives atlas independence, continuity of every induced map, and the quotient-topology criterion. Smoothness of $q$ implies flatness and local finite presentation by the chartwise calculus, so the openness clause of the topology node applies to $V\to\mathcal X$. Surjectivity follows from the field-extension local lifting clause of the calculus applied to the surjective atlas: every representative of a stack point lifts after a field extension. Thus $|q|$ is an open surjection. Taking complements in the open-set criterion gives the same criterion for closed sets.

A point of $R=V\times_{\mathcal X}V$ gives two points with equal image in $|\mathcal X|$. Conversely step 1 applied to this square lifts every pair with equal image to $|R|$. Therefore the image relation of $(|s|,|t|)$ is precisely equality of the $|q|$-images, hence an equivalence relation whose classes are the fibres of $|q|$. A subset $D$ satisfies $|s|^{-1}D=|t|^{-1}D$ exactly when membership is constant on these fibres: one implication tests a lift of each pair, and the other uses $|q||s|=|q||t|$.

For a closed subset $C$ its inverse image is closed by continuity and is saturated by step 3. Conversely, for a closed invariant $D$, set $C=|q|(D)$. Saturation gives $|q|^{-1}C=D$, so $C$ is closed by the quotient criterion in the topology node. Surjectivity gives $|q|(|q|^{-1}C)=C$, proving that the two operations are inverse. This includes the empty and full subsets.

Fix closed $C$ and let $D=|q|^{-1}C$. Give $D\subseteq|V|$ its unique reduced closed subspace structure $Z\subseteq V$ by the reduced-support node. Since a closed subspace of a scheme is representable by a closed subscheme, $Z$ is a scheme. The same node says that the closed subspaces $Z_s=R\times_{s,V}Z$ and $Z_t=R\times_{t,V}Z$ have supports $|s|^{-1}D$ and $|t|^{-1}D$. The two projections $R\to V$ are smooth base changes of the atlas by the chartwise calculus; hence $Z_s\to Z$ and $Z_t\to Z$ are smooth. Both pullbacks are reduced by smooth ascent of reducedness. Their supports agree by step 4; uniqueness of the reduced closed subspace of $R$ now gives $Z_s=Z_t$ as closed subspaces, including their scheme structures. This is the necessary stronger invariance, rather than only set-theoretic invariance.

source.place: Tag 0509 (lemma-reduced-closed-substack), construction of Z and equality of its two pullbacks; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0GB3.

proof.text: Apply invariant closed-subspace descent to this $Z\subseteq V$ and the equality just proved. It gives a strictly full algebraic closed substack $\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathcal X$ with $\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal X}V=Z$ and smooth surjective atlas $Z\to\mathcal Z$. Since $Z$ is reduced, this is a reduced smooth chart. To check every other smooth scheme chart $W\to\mathcal Z$, take $P=W\times_{\mathcal Z}Z$. Its projection to $Z$ is smooth and its projection to $W$ is smooth surjective, by the chartwise calculus. Smooth ascent makes $P$ reduced and smooth surjective descent makes $W$ reduced. Thus the constructed substack is reduced in the intrinsic smooth-chart sense. Its underlying image is $C$: points of $\mathcal Z$ lift after a field extension to the atlas $Z$, whose image in $|\mathcal X|$ is exactly $|q|(D)=C$.

source.place: Tag 0509, descent and reducedness; missing chart-independence argument expanded using spaces-descent.tex Tag 0GB3.

proof.text: For uniqueness, suppose $\mathcal Z'$ is another reduced closed substack with underlying subset $C$. Its pullback $Z'=V\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z'$ is a closed subscheme of $V$ and a smooth scheme chart of $\mathcal Z'$, hence reduced. Step 1 identifies its support with $|q|^{-1}C=D$. The reduced-support uniqueness gives $Z'=Z$ as closed subspaces of $V$. Injectivity of the closed-substack descent bijection now gives $\mathcal Z'=\mathcal Z$. Strict fullness is understood throughout, so this is uniqueness as a substack rather than uniqueness of a chosen presentation.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_presentation_closed_subsets (k : Type u) [Field k] (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) : (∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of k))) (q : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F), IsSmoothModuliAtlas F U q → moduliSmoothPointTopology F = TopologicalSpace.coinduced (moduliAtlasPointMap q) inferInstance ∧ @IsOpenMap _ _ inferInstance (moduliSmoothPointTopology F) (moduliAtlasPointMap q) ∧ Function.Surjective (moduliAtlasPointMap q) ∧ (∀ x y : U.left, moduliAtlasPointMap q x = moduliAtlasPointMap q y ↔ ∃ r : ModuliPoints (moduliTwoFiberProduct q q), moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberFst q q) r = moduliSchemePoint U x ∧ moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd q q) r = moduliSchemePoint U y) ∧ (∃ e : {C : Set (ModuliPoints F) // @IsClosed _ (moduliSmoothPointTopology F) C} ≃ {D : Set U.left // IsClosed D ∧ moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberFst q q) ⁻¹' (moduliSchemePoint U '' D) = moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd q q) ⁻¹' (moduliSchemePoint U '' D)}, ∀ C, (e C).val = moduliAtlasPointMap q ⁻¹' C.val)) ∧ (∀ (G : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over (Spec (.of k)))), IsAlgebraicModuliStack G → ∀ f : BasedFunctor F G, @Continuous _ _ (moduliSmoothPointTopology F) (moduliSmoothPointTopology G) (moduliPointMap f)) ∧ (∀ C : Set (ModuliPoints F), @IsClosed _ (moduliSmoothPointTopology F) C → ∃! W : ClosedModuliSubstack F, Set.range (moduliPointMap W.inclusion) = C ∧ ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) W.category), IsSmoothModuliAtlas W.category T a → AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced T.left) ∧ (∀ (A : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (B : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (C : BasedCategory.{v₃, w₃} (Over (Spec (.of k)))), IsAlgebraicModuliStack A → IsAlgebraicModuliStack B → IsAlgebraicModuliStack C → ∀ (a : BasedFunctor A B) (c : BasedFunctor C B), (∀ (x : ModuliPoints A) (y : ModuliPoints C), moduliPointMap a x = moduliPointMap c y → ∃ z : ModuliPoints (moduliTwoFiberProduct a c), moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberFst a c) z = x ∧ moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd a c) z = y) ∧ Set.range (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd a c)) = moduliPointMap c ⁻¹' Set.range (moduliPointMap a))
